clue.text: Rash involvement by swindler

indicators.note: an involvement is a tangle, so the letters of rash are twisted into a new order

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: A con man is accused of being caught up in some reckless scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like the adjective reckless, but its letters are the fodder that 'involvement' tangles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharper is a cheat, especially a card cheat, so a synonym of a con artist.

clue.text: Balance 'ready ? Let's have a break !

indicators.note: letters that have a break are broken up and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Someone at work calls out that it is time for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have a break' shuffles READY and LETS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is a weighing device with a sliding weight on a graduated arm, a type of scales.

clue.text: Instruction for pianist — also mountain-climber

parts.note: and means also, in addition

indicators.note: in a down clue something that climbs reads upwards, so the mountain's letters go backwards

parts.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Someone offers both a piano tutorial and a guide for mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' reverses ETNA to ANTE beneath AND in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Through the previous, one becomes an actor

parts.note: per means through or by means of
the former is the earlier of two mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a thespian by way of earlier experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is anyone who entertains on stage, including a thespian.

clue.text: Busy time in the plant?

explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory with a busy shift, but it is the reedlike marsh plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush is a hectic period, as in the rush hour, and also a marsh plant with stiff stems.

clue.text: Decline to swallow a simple drink

indicators.note: one word swallowing another takes it inside, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: the sun declines when it sets, so decline means set
a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to gulp down an uncomplicated beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' is a noun here, a medicinal plant, not an adjective describing the drink; 'Decline' is the sun setting, not refusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a sweet fruit beverage, originally Middle Eastern, so a kind of drink.

clue.text: Puts an end to mirth aboard, apparently

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, which crosswords show by putting letters within SS, the steamship abbreviation

parts.note: aboard is crossword shorthand for inside SS, the steamship abbreviation; 'apparently' admits the ship is only implied
laughter is mirth or merriment

explanation.surface: Something kills off all the fun on a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: SS is the standard abbreviation for a steamship; 'apparently' admits the laughter sits aboard one.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughters means kills, ending the lives of many.

clue.text: She has two letters written

parts.note: letters written out as words: the letter L is spelt ell
the second letter written out is N, spelt en

explanation.surface: A woman has penned a couple of notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' means alphabet letters spelt out, L and N, not correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's first name, so a 'she'.

clue.text: Producing 10 lines, for example, about victory

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the railway lines

indicators.note: about means around, so the example's letters surround the victory

parts.note: EG abbreviates the Latin for 'for example'
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: Someone produces ten lines of verse about a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SMALL BEER, so 'Producing 10' means making ale; 'lines' are railway lines, BR.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewing is the making of ale, including weak small beer.

clue.text: 17 would fill in these conditions

explanation.walkthrough: 17 is CLASSROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Classrooms fill during school terms, the sessions of the academic year; terms also means stipulations, as in the terms of a contract.

clue.text: The continental types of tree

parts.note: two European versions of the word 'the': Spanish el
the second version of 'the' is German der

explanation.surface: Someone asks what sorts of tree grow on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' points to mainland Europe: Spanish EL and German DER are both 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a small shrubby tree bearing white flowers and dark berries.

clue.text: Half a pint ? But it could fill a quart pot

definitions.text: Half a pint ? But it could fill a quart pot

parts.words: Half a pint ? But it could fill a quart pot
parts.note: a modest measure of ale, half a pint, is a small drink; yet weak table ale was brewed by the gallon and could fill a far bigger vessel

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase also means something trivial; the clue plays on the literal weak ale, which in volume could easily fill a quart (two-pint) pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is weak, low-alcohol ale, and figuratively anything of little importance.

clue.text: Jack Johnson's poem

explanation.surface: The boxer Jack Johnson is credited with writing a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Jack Johnson the boxer; split it: Jack is the American novelist, and Johnson is Dr Samuel Johnson, whose 1738 poem is called 'London'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London wrote The Call of the Wild; Samuel Johnson wrote a satirical poem named after the English capital.

clue.text: Business establishments of the time, since reorganized

parts.note: an age is a period of time, as in 'the age of steam'

indicators.note: the word since is reorganized, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Commercial firms that were founded long ago have since been restructured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the time' reads as old-established, but 'the time' is a period, and 'since' is fodder, not a time word.
explanation.definitionFit: Agencies are firms providing a service, such as travel or advertising offices.

clue.text: Game companion takes part ?

parts.note: a mate in games, also read as a chap who takes a role in a stage show

explanation.walkthrough: The play-mate sense is the definition; the question mark admits the second picture of a fellow in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A playfellow is a childhood companion one plays with, a playmate.

clue.text: A timber on one side of a ship

definitions.text: on one side of a ship

parts.note: taken as written
a beam is a long piece of timber

explanation.surface: A length of wood lies along one side of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is a nautical term for at right angles to the keel, level with the vessel's flank.

clue.text: Teach girl, sort of sluggish .

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them, so the words teach girl are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A tutor describes a pupil as rather lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means drowsy and without energy, a synonym of slow-moving.

clue.text: Unions can possibly separate friends

indicators.note: to separate a word is to split it apart, so the friends' letters go either side of the other piece

parts.note: allies are friends on the same side

indicators.note: possibly signals the word can is rearranged

explanation.surface: Trade unions might split comrades apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles 'can', and that jumble sits inside the friends, splitting them in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliances are unions or associations formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Rank or perhaps order in school

definitions.text: Rank or perhaps order in school

parts.words: Rank or perhaps order in school
parts.note: a rank or an order is a 'class'; the place in school where such a group sits

explanation.walkthrough: Both 'rank' and 'order' can mean a class, and the space a school class occupies is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A classroom is the room in which a school class is taught.

clue.text: Ship breaker?

explanation.walkthrough: 'breaker' suggests a ship-breaker's yard, but it simply means one who breaks things.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast naval warship, and literally anyone who wrecks or smashes things.

clue.text: Seven knights of the Orient

parts.note: Japanese warriors of the feudal era, seven of them in Kurosawa's famous film

explanation.walkthrough: Kurosawa's 1954 film is named after seven such swordsmen hired to defend a village.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan, likened to knights.

clue.text: Sorceress finds Asian priest about one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the priest's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk of Tibet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A witch encounters a Tibetan monk somewhere around one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamia is a witch or female demon of classical myth, preying on children.

clue.text: Coleridge's hero and Eliot's appearing around one

indicators.note: around means the novelist's character surrounds the other piece

parts.note: George Eliot wrote the novel Silas Marner
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Two poets' heroes are seen together around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliot's' looks like T. S. Eliot the poet, but it is George Eliot's weaver Silas MARNER, with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner has an old sailor as its central figure.

clue.text: He suffered a classic hang- over

definitions.text: He suffered a classic hang- over

parts.words: He suffered a classic hang- over
parts.note: a hangover after drinking, read instead as a sword hanging over a man's head in a Greek legend

explanation.walkthrough: In the legend the courtier sat at a feast beneath a sword hung by a single hair, so something classic was hanging over him.
explanation.definitionFit: Damocles is the Syracusan courtier who dined under a sword suspended by one hair.

clue.text: Put off from the Ambleside ferry?

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Someone postpones the crossing on the boat leaving the Lakeland town of Ambleside.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambleside is a town on Windermere in the English Lake District, where ferries run.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to postpone or delay, a synonym of put back.

clue.text: Berry a young creature appears to be raising

parts.note: a cub is the young of a fox, bear or lion

indicators.note: raising lifts a word up, which in a down clue means reading it from the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone named Berry seems to be bringing up a baby animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berry' looks like a person's name but is the definition; in a down light 'raising' reads the little verb from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubeb is the spicy dried berry of a Javanese pepper plant.

clue.text: Hebridean boatman ?

explanation.walkthrough: The Outer Hebrides are islands off north-west Scotland; Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel follows J, George and Harris on a boat trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris is an island of the Outer Hebrides; Harris is also one of the trio rowing on the Thames in Jerome's Three Men in a Boat.

clue.text: Hesitate to reveal identity of goddess?

definitions.text: Hesitate to reveal identity of goddess?

parts.words: Hesitate to reveal identity of goddess?
parts.note: a stammering speaker, reluctant to say who someone is, repeats a two-letter verb twice; that halting repetition names an Egyptian deity

explanation.walkthrough: Picture someone stalling before naming who a person is, repeating the same little verb; written down, the stammer is the name of the Egyptian goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis is the Egyptian goddess of motherhood and magic.

clue.text: Wood labels pieces of meteors

parts.note: fir is a softwood timber from conifers

indicators.note: breaking the word labels into pieces lets its letters be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tags made of timber are attached to fragments of fallen space rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood labels' suggests timber tags, but 'Wood' is a conifer and 'pieces' breaks up the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fireballs are exceptionally bright meteors, burning shooting stars.

clue.text: Many always active by the river.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
on, as in 'on and on', means continuing without stopping
go means working or ready, as in 'all systems go'

explanation.surface: Lots of people are always busy beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always active' recalls the phrase 'on the go'; the river is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo is the great river of central Africa.

clue.text: Heavenly sight made Words- worth's heart leap up

definitions.text: Heavenly sight made Words- worth's heart leap up

parts.words: Heavenly sight made Words- worth's heart leap up
parts.note: a coloured arc in the sky that, in the poet's lines, set his heart leaping

explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's poem begins 'My heart leaps up when I behold' this sight in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured arc appearing in the sky after rain is a heavenly sight in the literal sense.

clue.text: Name of ancient rattle suits Mr Turner ?

indicators.note: a turner turns things round, so the letters of suits Mr are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: An old musical rattle is said to please the painter J. M. W. Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter, but it is the anagram signal for SUITSMR.
explanation.definitionFit: The sistrum is a metal rattle used in ancient Egyptian worship.
